newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-GLAMORGAN SINK TO 31 ALL OUT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GLAMORGAN SINK TO 31 ALL OUT.

text.p: Glamorgan crashed to an embarrassing 31 all out, the lowest total in an English county championship match for 14 years, to lose by an innings and seven runs to Middlesex in Cardiff on Saturday.
Seamers Jamie Hewitt and Angus Fraser turned the match on its head on the third day, firing out Glamorgan for the fourth lowest total in their history in just 96 balls.
Former England bowler Fraser took four for 17 and Hewitt a career-best six for 14, as Glamorgan fared worse than any side since Surrey scored just 14 all out against Essex in 1983.
"When you think about it, just a couple of weeks ago we scored our highest total in the championship of 597 on this same ground. It's all a bit crazy," said Glamorgan captain Matthew Maynard.
"We had a couple of shooters along the deck, but the trouble with this game is that you never know what is going to happen."
The previous two days had given no hint of the drama to come with Glamorgan making 281 in their first innings and Middlesex reaching 247 for five at the close on Friday.
At 11 for six, Glamorgan threatened to go below their lowest-ever total of 22 against Lancashire at Liverpool in 1924.
But Anthony Cottey's 12 carried them beyond that mark, and two other embarrassing results. In 1971 Glamorgan were dismissed for 24 by Leicestershire and they made 26 against Lancashire in 1958.
Kevan James claimed a career-best eight for 49 to dismiss Somerset for 225, giving Hampshire an unlikely nine-run win.
Somerset appeared to be heading for an easy victory at 175 for three, but James cleaned up the rest of the innings to carry his side to a sensational victory.
Ashley Cowan finished with career-best match figures of nine for 123 as Essex recorded their second successive championship win with over a day to spare against Sussex.
Cowan, who took five for 45 in the first innings, collected four for 78 as Sussex were dismissed for 356 for a lead of 112 runs.
Essex openers Graham Gooch (51 not out) and Paul Prichard (54 not out) put on unbroken stand of 115 to carry their side to a 10-wicket victory.
